clue.text: It's warmer in bed

parts.note: a cryptic description of the rubber container filled from the kettle and tucked under the covers on a cold night

explanation.definitionFit: This rubber flask, filled from the kettle, is the classic British way to heat sheets before sleeping.

clue.text: Revolutionary centre starts bubbling with confused clamour.

parts.note: the hub is the centre of a revolving wheel

indicators.note: the opening run of the word bubbling is taken, as the word starts

explanation.surface: Something at the centre of a revolution begins to bubble amid noisy chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes the opening three letters of 'bubbling', BUB, not just its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A din of many voices is a noisy, muddled uproar.

clue.text: It's one Scotch and barleywater, please

parts.note: 'tis is the old contraction of it is
ane is the Scots word for one

explanation.surface: A customer orders a whisky and a soft drink at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like the whisky but says the word for 'one' is in Scots. The drink was first a barley decoction (ptisan).
explanation.definitionFit: The herbal infusion takes its name from the Greek ptisane, a drink of pearl barley.

clue.text: Period of solar decline.

parts.note: the stretch of the day when the sun is past its height and sinking

explanation.definitionFit: The part of the day after midday is when the sun descends from its zenith.

clue.text: A silver coat in current style?

definitions.text: A silver coat in current style?

parts.words: A silver coat in current style?
parts.note: current is electric current, which deposits a thin silver layer on cutlery, not a fashionable garment

explanation.definitionFit: Plating by electrolysis lays a film of silver on a base metal using electricity.

clue.text: See 1
Some know a hawk from a handsaw in Nebraska

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase are used, a run lying inside it

explanation.surface: Hamlet's line about knowing a hawk from a handsaw, transplanted to the American Midwest.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a place found in Nebraska.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest city of that Midwestern state sits on the Missouri river.

clue.text: Can't see the wood for the trees, Tim? Could be the reason

definitions.text: Can't see the wood for the trees, Tim? Could be the reason

indicators.note: the letters of the two words could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Someone mocks Tim with the proverb about missing the big picture.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle TREES and TIM. Read whole, the clue says wood-eating insects are why no wood is left among the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: White ants eat timber, so they are why wood may vanish from inside trees.

clue.text: Finishes belatedly but in high spirits

indicators.note: the word belatedly finishes with the run wanted, all but its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone finishes late but is cheerful about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something joyfully and with exhilaration is acting cheerfully.

clue.text: Best to get out of the ring, boy, when intoxicated

indicators.note: the letters are knocked out of their order, like a boxer leaving the ring

parts.note: Ed is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boxer, the boy, had better leave the ring while drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get out of the ring' shuffles BEST TO into BESOTT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stupefied with drink is the old sense; infatuated is the newer one.

clue.text: Lizards from an old city in Asia perhaps

indicators.note: the old city goes inside the rearranged letters
Asia perhaps signals its letters in a different order

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Reptiles from an ancient Asian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns ASIA into SA..IA, and 'in' places UR inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauria is the zoological suborder of reptiles that includes lizards.

clue.text: Like the Wild Man of Borneo to H.E.'s despair?

definitions.text: Like the Wild Man of Borneo to H.E.'s despair?

parts.words: Like the Wild Man of Borneo to H.E.'s despair?
parts.note: H.E. is His Excellency, the colonial governor, who cannot bring the wild man under rule

explanation.definitionFit: Something unruly cannot be controlled, which would dismay a colonial administrator.

clue.text: The beautiful Narcissus appears a little bony

indicators.note: only a little of the phrase is used, the run that appears across the two words

explanation.surface: Narcissus, the beauty of myth, looks rather skinny.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective relates to the forearm's inner long bone, so it is of a bone.

clue.text: Offer the unattainable in Tartarus

parts.note: in the Greek underworld, water and fruit forever just out of reach were offered to the punished king Tantalus

explanation.definitionFit: To tease with something always kept out of reach is the punishment of Tantalus.

clue.text: Flower with which the wise man made an impression ?

definitions.meaning: a woodland plant with arching stems and white bell flowers

definitions.text: with which the wise man made an impression
definitions.meaning: King Solomon, famed for wisdom, would press his signet into wax

explanation.definitionFit: Both a garden plant (Polygonatum) and the signet ring of the biblical king noted for wisdom.

clue.text: Bob had a rake in his hand-or a bird

parts.note: bob is slang for a shilling, abbreviated s in old British money
had in his hand means held
a garden rake, as written

explanation.surface: A gardener named Bob stood holding a rake, or was it a bird?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' is not a man but the old British shilling (s). 'in his hand' makes 'had' mean held.
explanation.definitionFit: This large duck of coasts and estuaries has bold chestnut and white plumage.

clue.text: With which Holmes's autocrat got cracking?

definitions.text: With which Holmes's autocrat got cracking?

parts.words: With which Holmes's autocrat got cracking?
parts.note: Oliver Wendell Holmes wrote The Autocrat of the Breakfast-Table, so cracking means opening a boiled one at breakfast

explanation.definitionFit: A small utensil for eating a soft-boiled breakfast item from its shell.

clue.text: Such is the art, or the crime maybe, of the alchemist

indicators.note: the crime maybe is a hint that those letters can be shaken into another order

explanation.surface: Alchemy is described as either an art or a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The hermetic art is alchemy, named after Hermes Trismegistus.
explanation.definitionFit: Alchemy was called the Hermetic art after Hermes Trismegistus, its legendary founder.

clue.text: Colourful covers for Elizabethan pop records?

definitions.text: Colourful covers for Elizabethan pop records?

parts.words: Colourful covers for Elizabethan pop records?
parts.note: verdant arm coverings, read as record sleeves, name a hit tune of Tudor England

explanation.definitionFit: The Tudor folk song, often linked to Henry VIII, was the popular melody of its age.

clue.text: Does the crossword variety have a bit of an urge to read dictionaries?

definitions.text: Does the crossword variety have a bit of an urge to read dictionaries?

indicators.note: only a bit of the phrase is used, a run across the two words

explanation.surface: Do crossword fans have some urge to read dictionaries?
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans 'read' and 'dictionaries'; the whole clue describes the puzzle fanatic.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword fiend is one hooked on a habit, often poring over dictionaries.

clue.text: One of the more eager mourners?

definitions.text: One of the more eager mourners?

parts.words: One of the more eager mourners?
parts.note: more eager is a comparative, but an Irish professional wailer at a funeral has the same name

explanation.definitionFit: A hired Irish wailer at funerals shares a name with the comparative of eager.

clue.text: Herb has style, but few brains

definitions.note: a noun phrase for a person who has few brains

parts.note: a simple is an old word for a medicinal herb
ton is fashionable style

explanation.surface: A man called Herb is stylish but dim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' looks like a name but is a plant, a simple; 'ton' (French) is high fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A foolish person lacks intelligence.

clue.text: Nothing particular to do at this end

definitions.text: Nothing particular to do at this end

parts.words: Nothing particular to do at this end
parts.note: the phrase at a ___ end means having nothing to occupy one

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'at a ___ end' describes being idle with no task in hand.

clue.text: Kansas City? One to avoid!

definitions.meaning: the Wild West cattle town in Kansas
a trick or evasion; to sidestep

explanation.definitionFit: Dodge City is the frontier town in Kansas; a dodge is also an evasion.

clue.text: A fine choice perhaps

parts.note: a court may give the alternative of paying money rather than going to prison

explanation.definitionFit: Being allowed to pay a penalty instead of jail is an alternative offered to the accused.

clue.text: Sacrifice of a boot-nail

indicators.note: the result is made of a boot-nail, its letters reformed

explanation.surface: A soldier offers up a boot-nail to the gods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of a' says the answer is made of BOOTNAIL rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An offering presented to a god is a sacrifice.

clue.text: One who pinches a quid?

definitions.meaning: a thief; to nick is to steal
British slang for a pound sterling

explanation.definitionFit: A thief nicks things; nicker is also British slang for one pound.

clue.text: Direction to put a shilling in the meter this term

parts.note: SE is south-east, a compass direction

indicators.note: the shilling is put in the meter

parts.note: a meter, as written
s is the abbreviation for a shilling in old British money

explanation.surface: A notice tells you to feed the meter a shilling for this period.
explanation.walkthrough: Put S inside METER after ME to make MESTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-year teaching period at college is one academic term.
